name: pdk-parsimonious-etl
instr:
Our validation jobs load their grammars with parsimonious (the checkout in /app). The language team now writes every grammar in the PEG notation of Bryan Ford's 2004 paper, since the same files feed their C tools, and Grammar() rejects them. Some of them are in /data/peg, each with a folder of the same name holding texts it must accept. peg.peg is the notation's own grammar, and every .peg file there has to parse with it.

Please make Grammar() take that notation as it is: rules defined with `<-`, `'...'` and `"..."` literals and `[...]` classes with the paper's escapes, and `.`. A grammar written that way must load and parse exactly as the same grammar written in parsimonious's notation would, with the same rules matching the same spans of every text and the same errors. Classes and `.` should also work, the same way, in parsimonious's own notation. A grammar that uses both `=` and `<-`, or a class with a reversed range such as `[z-a]`, should raise BadGrammar.

We send merged grammars back to the team, so str() of a grammar loaded from that notation (also after .default()) has to print it in the paper's notation, in a form that loads back into the same grammar.

Grammars in parsimonious's notation have to load, parse and print exactly as they do now, and the existing tests in /app/parsimonious/tests have to keep passing. There's no network here, and the package is installed in editable mode in /opt/venv.
